hello.note: Many people just say the English "hello". Answering the phone: 喂 (wai2).

goodbye.note: In daily life most people say 拜拜 (baai1 baai3).

please.note: Goes before a request. Inviting someone ("please, go ahead"): 請 (cing2).

thank_you.note: For gifts and compliments. For a service or small favour, say 唔該 (m4 goi1).

youre_welcome.note: After 唔該, the reply is 唔使唔該 (m4 sai2 m4 goi1). Casual: 唔使 (m4 sai2).

yes.note: Often you answer with the verb instead: 有 (jau5) "have", 得 (dak1) "can", 好 (hou2) "OK".

no.note: Or negate the verb: 冇 (mou5) "don't have". Turning down an offer: 唔使喇 (m4 sai2 laa3).

sorry.note: For something minor, 唔好意思 (m4 hou2 ji3 si3) is lighter.

excuse_me.note: Then 請問 (cing2 man6) before your question. Squeezing past: 唔該借借 (m4 goi1 ze3 ze3).

good_morning.note: Said until about 11 a.m. Casual: 早 (zou2).

how_are_you.note: With people you know: 最近點呀？ (zeoi3 gan6 dim2 aa3?), how have you been?

im_fine.note: 幾 (gei2) here means "quite". Also common: 都唔錯 (dou1 m4 co3), "not bad".

whats_your_name.roman: cing2 man6 nei5 giu3 me1 meng2 aa3?
whats_your_name.note: More formal: 請問點稱呼？ (cing2 man6 dim2 cing1 fu1?), how should I address you?

my_name_is.note: Giving just your surname is common and polite: 我姓… (ngo5 sing3 …).

nice_to_meet_you.roman: hou2 gou1 hing3 sik1 dou2 nei5

where_from.roman: nei5 hai6 bin1 dou6 jan4 aa3?

im_from.note: Literally "I'm a … person": 我係英國人 (ngo5 hai6 jing1 gwok3 jan4), I'm British.

speak_english.text: 請問你識唔識講英文呀？
speak_english.roman: cing2 man6 nei5 sik1 m4 sik1 gong2 jing1 man2 aa3?
speak_english.note: 識唔識 (sik1 m4 sik1), "know or not know", is the usual way to ask "can you…?" about a skill.

dont_understand.note: When you heard but didn't follow: 我聽唔明 (ngo5 teng1 m4 ming4).

speak_slowly.roman: m4 goi1 nei5 gong2 maan6 di1

where.note: The bare word is 邊度 (bin1 dou6). Put the place first: 車站喺邊度？ (ce1 zaam6 hai2 bin1 dou6?)

what.note: Also 乜嘢 (mat1 je5). Didn't catch what someone said? 吓？ (haa2?)

when.note: Goes before the verb: 你幾時走？ (nei5 gei2 si4 zau2?), when are you leaving?

why.note: Casual: 做咩呀？ (zou6 me1 aa3?), "what for?"

who.note: Also means "which one": 邊個好啲？ (bin1 go3 hou2 di1?), which is better?

where_bathroom.roman: cing2 man6 sai2 sau2 gaan1 hai2 bin1 dou6?
where_bathroom.note: The plainer word is 廁所 (ci3 so2).

can_you_help.roman: nei5 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 bong1 haa5 ngo5 aa3?
can_you_help.note: To a stranger, start with 唔好意思 (m4 hou2 ji3 si3).

what_time.note: Answer: 三點 (saam1 dim2), three o'clock.

what_means.roman: ni1 go3 hai6 me1 ji3 si1?
what_means.note: 意思 is ji3 si1 when it means "meaning", but ji3 si3 in 唔好意思.

one.note: Prices and signs use the digits 1, 2, 3…; 一 二 三 are the written words.

two.note: Before a measure word it becomes 兩 (loeng5): 兩個 (loeng5 go3), two of them.

four.note: Sounds like 死 (sei2), "die", so 4 is thought unlucky.

five.note: A hummed ng sound with no vowel.

seven.note: Jyutping c sounds like the ch in "church".

eight.note: Rhymes with 發 (faat3), "prosper", so 8 is lucky.

ten.note: Eleven is 十一 (sap6 jat1); twenty is 二十 (ji6 sap6).

water.note: A glass of water, please: 唔該俾杯水我 (m4 goi1 bei2 bui1 seoi2 ngo5).

coffee.note: Iced coffee in a local café: 凍啡 (dung3 fe1).

tea.note: Hong Kong milk tea: 奶茶 (naai5 caa4). 飲茶 (jam2 caa4) means going for dim sum.

im_hungry.note: Starving: 我餓死喇 (ngo5 ngo6 sei2 laa3).

menu_please.roman: m4 goi1 bei2 go3 caan1 paai2 ngo5
menu_please.note: Many people just use the English word menu.

bill_please.note: Also written 買單. A writing gesture in the air works too.

delicious.note: For a drink: 好好飲！ (hou2 hou2 jam2!)

enjoy_meal.note: Literally "eat slowly", said by a host or waiter. Calling everyone to eat: 食飯喇 (sik6 faan6 laa3).

straight_ahead.note: To a taxi driver: 直去 (zik6 heoi3).

stop_here.note: On a minibus, call out 前面有落 (cin4 min6 jau5 lok6) to get off at the next stop.

hotel.note: In Hong Kong 酒店 means hotel, not a bar.

train_station.note: Metro (MTR) station: 地鐵站 (dei6 tit3 zaam6) or 港鐵站 (gong2 tit3 zaam6).

want_to_go.note: In a taxi, just say 唔該去… (m4 goi1 heoi3 …).

is_it_far.note: How long does it take? 要幾耐呀？ (jiu3 gei2 noi6 aa3?)

one_ticket.note: 飛 (fei1), from English "fare", is the everyday word for ticket; the formal one is 票 (piu3).

too_expensive.note: Softer: 貴咗啲 (gwai3 zo2 di1), "a bit pricey".

cheaper.note: Bargaining: 平啲得唔得呀？ (peng4 di1 dak1 m4 dak1 aa3?), can you do it cheaper?

id_like_this.roman: m4 goi1, ngo5 jiu3 ni1 go3

just_looking.note: Also: 睇下先 (tai2 haa5 sin1), "just having a look first".

pay_card.roman: ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 luk1 kaat1 aa3?
pay_card.note: 碌卡 (luk1 kaat1) is "swipe the card". The Octopus travel card is 八達通 (baat3 daat6 tung1).

open.note: Asking: 開咗門未呀？ (hoi1 zo2 mun4 mei6 aa3?), are you open yet?

closed.note: Said aloud: 閂咗門 (saan1 zo2 mun4), "it's shut".

small.note: Cantonese uses 細, not 小, for size. Size S: 細碼 (sai3 maa5).

tomorrow.note: Day after tomorrow: 後日 (hau6 jat6).

yesterday.note: Also written 尋日 and often said cam4 jat6.

now.note: Often said ji1 gaa1, and also written 依家.

later.note: Later today, in a while: 陣間 (zan6 gaan1).

good_evening.note: Formal, e.g. on TV; it also means good night. In daily life people just say 你好 (nei5 hou2).

good_night.note: Literally "rest early". 晚安 (maan5 on1) is also used.

see_you_later.note: If it's within the hour: 一陣見 (jat1 zan6 gin3).

wait_moment.note: Quick and casual: 等等 (dang2 dang2).

need_doctor.note: Call an ambulance: 叫白車 (giu3 baak6 ce1).

dont_feel_well.roman: ngo5 m4 hai6 hou2 syu1 fuk6
dont_feel_well.note: Stronger: 我好唔舒服 (ngo5 hou2 m4 syu1 fuk6).

lost_phone.roman: ngo5 m4 gin3 zo2 bou6 sau2 gei1
lost_phone.note: Also: 我跌咗部手機 (ngo5 dit3 zo2 bou6 sau2 gei1). 部 (bou6) is the counter for phones.

allergic.note: E.g. 我對花生敏感 (ngo5 deoi3 faa1 sang1 man5 gam2), I'm allergic to peanuts.

of_course.note: Very colloquial: 梗係啦！ (gang2 hai6 laa1!)

i_like_it.note: 鍾意 is also written 中意.

welcome.note: To a guest at home, add 入嚟坐啦 (jap6 lai4 co5 laa1), come in and sit down.

congratulations.note: Warmer: 恭喜晒 (gung1 hei2 saai3). At Lunar New Year: 恭喜發財 (gung1 hei2 faat3 coi4).

my_family.note: 屋企 (uk1 kei2) on its own means "home". More formal: 我嘅家人 (ngo5 ge3 gaa1 jan4).

mother.note: Talking about her: 阿媽 (aa3 maa1). Younger people also say 媽咪 (maa1 mi4).

father.note: Very common for "my dad": 老豆 (lou5 dau6). Also 爹哋 (de1 di4).

brother.note: Older brother, also 阿哥 (aa3 go1). Younger brother: 細佬 (sai3 lou2).

sister.note: Older sister. Younger sister: 細妹 (sai3 mui2).

child.note: Son: 仔 (zai2); daughter: 女 (neoi2). A kid in general is 細路 (sai3 lou6).

friend.note: Same for a woman. But 男朋友 (naam4 pang4 jau5) is a boyfriend, 女朋友 (neoi5 pang4 jau5) a girlfriend.

this_is_my_friend.roman: ni1 go3 hai6 ngo5 pang4 jau5
this_is_my_friend.note: Same for a female friend. More polite: 呢位係我朋友 (ni1 wai2 hai6 ngo5 pang4 jau5).

are_you_married.roman: nei5 git3 zo2 fan1 mei6 aa3?
are_you_married.note: Literally "married yet?" Answers: 結咗喇 (git3 zo2 laa3), yes; 未呀 (mei6 aa3), not yet.

have_children.roman: nei5 jau5 mou5 zai2 neoi2 aa3?
have_children.note: Answer 有 (jau5), yes, or 冇 (mou5), no.

monday.note: The days are numbered from Monday. Also very common: 禮拜一 (lai5 baai3 jat1).

tuesday.note: Here 二 stays ji6, never 兩. Also 禮拜二 (lai5 baai3 ji6).

sunday.note: Ends in 日 (jat6), "day", not a number. Also 禮拜日 (lai5 baai3 jat6).

weekend.note: In everyday talk also 星期六日 (sing1 kei4 luk6 jat6), "Saturday and Sunday".

what_day.roman: gam1 jat6 sing1 kei4 gei2 aa3?
what_day.note: 幾 (gei2), "how many", stands in for the number. Answer: 星期五 (sing1 kei4 ng5).

next_week.note: Also 下個禮拜 (haa6 go3 lai5 baai3). Last week: 上個星期 (soeng6 go3 sing1 kei4).

twelve.note: Even before a counter it stays 二: 十二個 (sap6 ji6 go3), twelve of them.

fifteen.note: Clock minutes are counted in fives: 三點三 (saam1 dim2 saam1) means 3:15.

twenty.note: In the twenties people say 廿 (jaa6): 廿五 (jaa6 ng5), 25.

thirty.note: In quick speech 十 shrinks to aa6: 三十五 (35) sounds like saam1 aa6 ng5.

fifty.note: Fifty dollars: 五十蚊 (ng5 sap6 man1). 蚊 (man1) is the everyday word for dollar.

hundred.note: Prices drop the end: 百五 (baak3 ng5) means 150.

thousand.note: Ten thousand has its own word: 一萬 (jat1 maan6).

how_old.roman: nei5 gam1 nin4 gei2 do1 seoi3 aa3?
how_old.note: To an older person: 你今年貴庚呀？ (nei5 gam1 nin4 gwai3 gang1 aa3?) To a child: 你幾歲呀？ (nei5 gei2 seoi3 aa3?)

years_old.note: No verb needed: 我今年三十歲 (ngo5 gam1 nin4 saam1 sap6 seoi3), I'm thirty.

red.note: 色 (sik1) means "colour". Red is lucky: think of the red packet, 利是 (lai6 si6).

blue.note: Dark blue: 深藍色 (sam1 laam4 sik1). Light blue: 淺藍色 (cin2 laam4 sik1).

green.note: Never give a green hat: 戴綠帽 (daai3 luk6 mou2) means being cheated on.

yellow.note: Also means "X-rated": 黃色笑話 (wong4 sik1 siu3 waa2) is a dirty joke.

black.note: Black coffee, though, is 齋啡 (zaai1 fe1), "plain coffee".

white.note: White is the colour of funerals, so avoid white flowers or gift wrap.

what_colour.roman: ni1 go3 hai6 me1 ngaan4 sik1 aa3?
what_colour.note: In speech often shortened: 咩色呀？ (me1 sik1 aa3?)

this_one.note: 個 (go3) is the general counter. For clothes use 件 (gin6): 呢件 (ni1 gin6).

that_one.note: 嗰 (go2), "that", and the counter 個 (go3) differ only in tone.

another_one.roman: m4 goi1 zoi3 lai4 jat1 go3
another_one.note: 嚟 (lai4), "come", is the usual ordering verb. For a drink: 再嚟一杯 (zoi3 lai4 jat1 bui1).

its_hot.note: Sweltering: 熱到死 (jit6 dou3 sei2), literally "hot to death".

its_cold.note: Cantonese mostly uses 凍 (dung3) for cold; 冷 (laang5) is also heard.

its_raining.note: 緊 (gan2) means it's happening now. Pouring: 落大雨 (lok6 daai6 jyu5).

its_sunny.note: Literally "very big sun". When the sun comes out: 出太陽喇 (ceot1 taai3 joeng4 laa3).

its_windy.note: When a typhoon hits: 打風 (daa2 fung1).

weather_today.roman: gam1 jat6 tin1 hei3 dim2 aa3?
weather_today.note: Will it rain? 會唔會落雨呀？ (wui5 m4 wui5 lok6 jyu5 aa3?)

beautiful_day.note: 好天 (hou2 tin1) means fine weather; the first 好 means "very".

umbrella.note: 雨傘 (jyu5 saan3) is the written word, but people say 遮. Take an umbrella: 帶遮 (daai3 ze1).

summer.note: In speech also 熱天 (jit6 tin1), "the hot days".

winter.note: In speech also 冷天 (laang5 tin1), "the cold days".

have_reservation.note: Then give your surname: 我姓… (ngo5 sing3 …). At a restaurant: 我訂咗枱 (ngo5 deng6 zo2 toi2).

room.note: Often just 房 (fong2): 單人房 (daan1 jan4 fong2), single room.

passport.note: Hong Kong ID card: 身份證 (san1 fan2 zing3).

wifi_password.roman: cing2 man6 Wi-Fi mat6 maa5 hai6 me1 aa3?
wifi_password.note: Wi-Fi is written in English and said "wai-fai". Is there Wi-Fi? 有冇Wi-Fi呀？ (jau5 mou5 Wi-Fi aa3?)

check_out_time.roman: cing2 man6 gei2 dim2 jiu3 teoi3 fong2 aa3?
check_out_time.note: Many people say check out in English: 幾點check out呀？ (gei2 dim2 check out aa3?)

bus.note: Minibus: 小巴 (siu2 baa1). Getting off is 落車 (lok6 ce1).

next_train.roman: haa6 jat1 baan1 fo2 ce1 gei2 dim2 hoi1 aa3?
next_train.note: 班 (baan1) is the counter for scheduled trains and buses. On the MTR just say 車 (ce1).

is_this_seat_free.text: 請問呢個位有冇人坐呀？
is_this_seat_free.roman: cing2 man6 ni1 go3 wai2 jau5 mou5 jan4 co5 aa3?
is_this_seat_free.note: Literally "is anyone sitting in this seat?" Reply if it's free: 冇人 (mou5 jan4).

what_do_you_do.roman: cing2 man6 nei5 zou6 bin1 hong4 gaa3?
what_do_you_do.note: Literally "which trade are you in?" Also 你做咩工㗎？ (nei5 zou6 me1 gung1 gaa3?)

i_work_in.note: For a place, e.g. 我喺銀行做嘢 (ngo5 hai2 ngan4 hong4 zou6 je5). For a field: 我做銷售 (ngo5 zou6 siu1 sau6).

im_student.note: Same for a woman. University student: 大學生 (daai6 hok6 saang1).

office.note: The workplace or office building. A single office room: 辦公室 (baan6 gung1 sat1).

meeting.note: In speech: 我開緊會 (ngo5 hoi1 gan2 wui2), I'm in a meeting.

im_busy.note: No time right now: 我唔得閒 (ngo5 m4 dak1 haan4). Swamped: 忙到飛起 (mong4 dou3 fei1 hei2).

day_off.note: I'm off today: 我今日放假 (ngo5 gam1 jat6 fong3 gaa3). Asking for leave: 請假 (cing2 gaa3).

lets_start.note: Casual, to a team: 開工啦！ (hoi1 gung1 laa1!), let's get to work.

good_job.note: Also 好嘢！ (hou2 je5!), great! Praising someone's skill: 好叻！ (hou2 lek1!)

table_for_two.note: Literally "two people, please", said as you walk in. 位 (wai2) is the polite counter for people.

what_recommend.roman: jau5 me1 hou2 gaai3 siu6 aa3?
what_recommend.note: Literally "anything good to introduce?" The house speciality: 招牌菜 (ziu1 paai4 coi3).

not_spicy.note: Ordering shorthand: 走辣 (zau2 laat6). A little spicy: 小辣 (siu2 laat6).

vegetarian_food.note: Also 齋 (zaai1): 有冇齋菜呀？ (jau5 mou5 zaai1 coi3 aa3?), any vegetarian dishes?

more_water.note: Asks for a top-up, also of the teapot at dim sum. Another glass: 唔該俾多杯水我 (m4 goi1 bei2 do1 bui1 seoi2 ngo5).

no_sugar.note: 走 (zau2), "leave", means "without" when ordering. Less sweet: 少甜 (siu2 tim4).

im_full.note: Also 我食飽喇 (ngo5 sik6 baau2 laa3). Really full: 好飽 (hou2 baau2).

takeaway.note: Also 外賣 (ngoi6 maai6). Eating in: 喺度食 (hai2 dou6 sik6).

it_was_delicious.note: No past tense needed. Casual praise: 好正！ (hou2 zeng3!), excellent!

keep_change.note: 找 (zaau2) means to give change. Many restaurants add a 10% service charge: 加一 (gaa1 jat1).

stomach.note: Diarrhoea: 肚屙 (tou5 ngo1). Feeling sick: 想嘔 (soeng2 ngau2).

head_hurts.note: Same pattern: 我肚痛 (ngo5 tou5 tung3), my stomach hurts; 我喉嚨痛 (ngo5 hau4 lung4 tung3), sore throat.

have_fever.note: Running a fever right now: 我發緊燒 (ngo5 faat3 gan2 siu1). A cold or flu: 感冒 (gam2 mou6).

medicine.note: Take medicine: 食藥 (sik6 joek6), literally "eat medicine".

call_ambulance.note: 白車 (baak6 ce1), "white car", is the everyday word for ambulance. Dial 999.

dentist.note: Going to the dentist: 睇牙 (tai2 ngaa4).

need_rest.note: Casual: 我要唞下 (ngo5 jiu3 tau2 haa5).

feel_better.note: 返 (faan1) after an adjective means "back to how it was".

get_well.note: To a friend: 快啲好返啦！ (faai3 di1 hou2 faan1 laa1!)

lets_meet.roman: bat1 jyu4 ceot1 lai4 gin3 haa5 min6 laa1
lets_meet.note: 不如 (bat1 jyu4), "how about", makes a friendly suggestion. Meeting for a meal: 約食飯 (joek3 sik6 faan6).

are_you_free.roman: nei5 ting1 jat6 dak1 m4 dak1 haan4 aa3?
are_you_free.note: 得閒 (dak1 haan4) means free. Reply 得閒 or 唔得閒 (m4 dak1 haan4).

call_me.roman: maa4 faan4 nei5 daa2 din6 waa2 bei2 ngo5
call_me.note: Casual: 打俾我啦 (daa2 bei2 ngo5 laa1). 俾 (bei2) here means "to".

your_number.roman: cing2 man6 nei5 din6 waa2 gei2 do1 hou6 aa3?
your_number.note: Numbers are read digit by digit; 0 is 零 (ling4).

see_you_soon.note: Literally "see you next time". Also 遲啲見 (ci4 di1 gin3). Later today: 一陣見 (jat1 zan6 gin3).

have_nice_day.roman: zuk1 nei5 gam1 jat6 hoi1 hoi1 sam1 sam1!
have_nice_day.note: No fixed everyday phrase. As you leave, hosts and shop staff say 慢慢行 (maan6 maan2 haang4), "take care".

good_luck.note: Before an exam or a match: 加油！ (gaa1 jau4!), literally "add oil".

thanks_a_lot.note: 晒 (saai3) adds "so much". For a favour or service: 唔該晒 (m4 goi1 saai3).

miss_you.note: 掛住 (gwaa3 zyu6) is the Cantonese word for missing someone. Homesick: 好掛住屋企 (hou2 gwaa3 zyu6 uk1 kei2).
